This is an explicitly informed follow-up diagnostic, not an unseen evaluation.
The previous direct-control attempt on this same initial condition completed 1000 steps but fell: its first code kept the initial reference for 50 steps; the next gradually crouched and shifted hip roll; a right-foot swing then used time interpolation, and later recovery failed. Those programs mostly used pelvis height as an early exit. A height-only guard did not stabilize the robot; stop returned control to the LLM, not an action that could reverse the fall.
Your task remains to stand, make controlled progress toward the ball, and kick if possible within 1000 total control steps. Design your own code; no working gait or action solution is supplied.
Use the new per-step feedback capability rather than repeating the previous open-loop right-leg swing. Consider a small posture calibration before lifting a foot; inspect pelvis quaternion/angular velocity, COM velocity, and contacts continuously. Determine correction signs from small reversible trials, bound corrections, slew-limit joint targets, and define stable settling criteria before entering a new phase. Do not assume that periodic joint curves produce a stable walking gait. Do not start larger motions merely because a timer elapsed while tilt or lateral velocity is growing.
The ankle COM aid is unchanged, runs at 500Hz, and assumes double support near the original heading. It is not a locomotion policy and may oppose a requested weight shift. Account for its observed offsets without accumulating them into nominal references. Your program runs at 50Hz and can coordinate hips, knees, waist, arms and ankles simultaneously; early done is available for handing back a segment.
Use initial_joint_reference_rad as a known starting reference, retain explicit nominal targets across segments, and inspect the actual state after each segment. If stable forward steps are not achievable, report that accurately; don't equate upright standing or a fall's displacement with walking. Continue meaningful control attempts within the episode budget, without resetting or changing physics.
